correctness.rationale: Exact reduction to a reversible degree-eight linear recurrence in the outer-ring indicator; factorization P_3=(t+1)^4 Phi_5 divides t^20+1, proving gcd(n,20)-periodicity. All 256 possible period-twenty words and six weight profiles are exhaustively enumerated by a standalone Python verifier; an independent full closed-neighborhood Gaussian-elimination implementation in C++ checks n=7..100 and brute-forces all subsets for n=7..10. The all-order theorem follows from polynomial divisibility, not finite extrapolation. The index-four comparison to step two is proved by comparing gcd annihilator degrees.

No inspected broader statement implies the seven-level twenty-period spectrum.

originality.rationale: The novelty assessed is the complete inhomogeneous parity-solution weight enumerator for GP(n,3) and, specifically, the index-four enlargement over GP(n,2) at 4|n and its seven-level twenty-period weights. The equality off multiples of four is a consequence of earlier GP(n,2) work and the new polynomial comparison and is not itself claimed as new. Fu–Yang–Jiang prove ordinary domination, Torrence–Torrence give generalized Lights Out nullities and strategies without all-on weights, Karami classifies parameter matrices of exact equitable two-colorings, and Wang–Zhang already classify the four optimal perfect codes when 4|n. The strongest directly known subclaim is explicitly excluded from the novelty assertion. Relevant papers were materially inspected; residual unindexed priority risk remains.
residual_risks: A complete parity-weight enumeration in unindexed or inaccessible older literature could cover the proposed new weight spectrum.
The ordinary domination and perfect-code results already settle some minima; those covered subclaims are not asserted to be original.
Only same-model scientific assessment has been performed; independent scholarly priority assessment remains open.

value.rationale: The all-on Lights Out strategy-weight distribution is a canonical natural invariant, simultaneously determining optimal move count, number and shape of optimum strategies, and every attainable nonoptimal cost. The step-three transition adds exactly a two-dimensional binary solution space to step two for multiples of four, and its interaction with the five-phase yields a previously uncovered seven-level twenty-period census with 192 genuinely new strategies. This is a structural infinite-family classification, not a parameter-free textbook restatement or one-off arbitrary finite slice. Known perfect-code minima are acknowledged as prior work.
